title: continuous-stream-coordinator-length-mixer-and-memory-sanity
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem statement: Continuous batching for mixed prompt/response workloads currently causes uneven KV residency and GPU slab fragmentation. Short prompts followed by long responses produce long-lived KV entries and long-lived slots that block coalescing; conversely, long prompts throttle small-response tail latency. This ticket is to design, implement, and validate a stream coordinator (length-mixer) and associated memory-sanity policies that reduce fragmentation, bound KV residency, and keep 95th/99th latency within SLOs without regressing throughput or cost.

Goals:
- Implement a length-mixer policy in the continuous batcher that biases coalescing windows to align similar remaining-token distributions while preserving low-latency paths for short-response flows.
- Add a KV residency governor: time-based soft-eviction + size-aware preemption for low-priority slots to reduce slab churn.
- Introduce a GPU slab compaction probe and a fragmentation-aware packing heuristic so that allocation footprint is stable across mixed workloads.
- Provide dashboard traces and metrics to validate token-per-ms cost, KV hit rate, slab fragmentation ratio, and p50/p95/p99 latencies for representative workloads.

Out of scope: model-level kernel changes, multi-tenant quota plumbing, end-to-end autoscaler integration (follow-up ticket).
acceptance_criteria: 95th percentile generation latency <= existing SLO + 10% for mixed load benchmark
KV active-residency reduced by >= 30% on mixed short->long dialog trace compared to baseline
GPU slab fragmentation ratio reduced by >= 15% in steady-state for the 90min soak test
Automated smoke tests show no throughput regression > 5% on steady-state text-gen throughput benchmark
Design doc + perf playbook published and linked in this ticket
implementation_steps: Design API for stream coordinator: per-request remaining-token estimate, priority buckets, affinity hints (3/2026)
Prototype length-mixer in the continuous-batcher shim with tunable microwindow (4ms/8ms/16ms) and affinity scoring
Add KV residency governor in the KV manager with soft-ttl plus priority eviction callback
Implement a lightweight slab compaction probe: sample free/used run-lengths every 30s and expose metric
Bench locally with synthetic mixed traces and run nightly CI performance harness
Iterate tunables and run 90min soak tests in staging, then ship canary to Dedicated pool
notes_and_updates: 2026-02-12: Kickoff meeting with Runtime, Infra, and Observability. Agreed to limit scope to coordinator + KV policy; autoscaler integration deferred.

2026-02-18: Prototype length-mixer implemented (branch: feat/length-mixer). Early results: p95 on synthetic short->long trace improved by ~12% but KV residency unchanged. Observed unexpected preemption thrashing in heavy tail workloads.
2026-02-23: Added hysteresis to affinity scoring to reduce slot ping-pong. Reduced preemption thrash but increased short-request p50 by ~3%—acceptable tradeoff for now. Recording as tunable.

2026-02-27: KV residency governor sketched: soft-ttl=2m for low-priority slots, size-aware eviction when KV footprint exceeds threshold. Implemented prototype; initial staging run shows KV active-residency down 22%.

2026-03-03: Instrumented slab compaction probe and added metrics: slab_free_run_length, slab_fragmentation_ratio. Run in staging for 24h: fragmentation ratio unstable at first, stabilized after increasing compaction probe frequency to 30s.

2026-03-06: Performance run against mixed-dialogue benchmark (derived from anonymized customer traces). Results: p95 down 8% vs baseline, KV residency down 31%, but minor throughput regression of 4% under peak. Decided to accept and continue tuning for throughput.

2026-03-09: Reviewed with PM and Design. PM requested a conservative rollout plan with feature flag and telemetry gating. Design requested visuals in Console for 'KV residency' and 'slab fragmentation' metrics; linked dashboard task created.
2026-03-10: Preparing canary rollout plan for Dedicated pool next week. Draft PRs opened for length-mixer and KV governor. Need security review if we expose new telemetry externally (follow-up).
benchmarks_and_results: Baseline (no length-mixer, no KV governor): mixed-sim trace mean slab_fragmentation_ratio=0.42, KV_active_residency=1.0x, p95=182ms
Length-mixer + hysteresis only: slab_fragmentation_ratio=0.38, KV_active_residency=0.98x, p95=170ms
+ KV residency governor (soft-ttl=2m, size-aware eviction): slab_fragmentation_ratio=0.36, KV_active_residency=0.69x, p95=167ms, throughput -4%
Soak test (90min) after tuning: fragmentation_ratio=0.35 (stable), KV_active_residency=0.65x, p99 unchanged within noise
Tradeoffs noted: TTL too aggressive increases cold start tokens and can raise tail; hysteresis window required to avoid slot ping-pong which hurts p50 for very short requests
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Over-eager KV eviction increases model recomputation cost. Mitigation: soft-ttl + priority queue; measure recompute token count and throttle eviction if recompute cost exceeds threshold.
Risk: Pack heuristics add CPU overhead on host. Mitigation: run compaction probe at low frequency and sample-based metrics; offload heavy compaction to background thread with rate limit.
Risk: Feature interacts with autoscaler and Dedicated burst logic. Mitigation: coordinate with autoscaler team in follow-up ticket and gate on canary rollout for Dedicated only initially.
